page.layout: One page of verse, one column, centred-left; running head at top; page number at top left; catchword at lower right. Faint show-through from the facing page on the right side is not transcribed.

main_text.p:
Vna perisset sorte passim
Victima nil miserantis unda.
Sed vir relictus coniuge cum pia est,
Cultor supremi Numinis integer,
Arca capaci clausus aluo,
Cum genitis nuribusque charis.
Successit istis orta parentibus
Terras per omnes gens habitabiles
Diffusa sol quacunque mundum
Limpidus irradiat patentem.
Lugenda chordis flebilibus mala
Frata summi dextera iudicis
Quae mittit, ut poenas nefandis
Criminibus meritas rependat.
Concussa motu Gallia civico
Paces quietas odit, & ocia
Vicina turbat, quin ruinam,
Dum ruit ipsa, aliis minatur.
Sic tecta tectis finitimis metus
Incensa magnos protinus afferunt:
Casura sic damnum propinquis
Arboribus meditatur arbos.
Nec sola bello Gallia concidit,
Sed dira cunctos cladibus horridis
Bellona mortales fatigat,
Funeribusque cruentat orbem,
Non ante seclis visa prioribus,
Et morte quouis horridior fames
Grassata

page.notes: The verse lines are printed as separate lines; the last word "Grassata" stands alone at the right, as a catchword-like closing word of the passage. Some letters in the scan are faint (e.g. "Victima", "Frata", "Arca") and read with some uncertainty; a few word forms may be printing variants.
